system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The supplied process-creation records show PowerShell running on WS-ICHEN-01 at 13:45 under sam.okafor, with the command to run the known Apply-Updates.ps1 path. They do not show that this was the window ivy reported around 13:40.

The PowerShell execution is consistent with the stated patching practice: shortly beforehand, WS-ICHEN-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01; the PowerShell command then downloaded from Windows Update and launched a Windows update package.
At 13:40, the supplied proxy records show ivy.chen's Chrome browser accessing Salesforce; those records do not identify PowerShell activity.

At 14:16, Explorer recorded a UserAssist registry value whose encoded path decodes to powershell.exe. This does not provide a command line or establish when the executable was launched, and the supplied records do not include a matching PowerShell process-creation event at that time.

The workstation made a DropboxUpdate-labeled proxy connection, and DropboxUpdate.exe later ran as SYSTEM. This is an unapproved service according to the supplied inventory context, but these records do not establish file synchronization or data transfer.
Google Drive File Stream ran in ivy.chen's user context. The supplied records show its process start but do not show whether it synchronized files or transferred data.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not show the user interface or establish whether a PowerShell window was visible to ivy.chen.
The UserAssist event records a registry value, not the PowerShell command line or a directly correlated process start.
The proxy records show connection metadata and some requested URLs, not the contents of encrypted application traffic or whether Dropbox or Google Drive synchronized files.
The available records do not establish the contents or integrity of Apply-Updates.ps1.
claims_not_established: That the PowerShell execution at 13:45 was the specific window ivy reported around 13:40.
That ivy.chen launched PowerShell at 13:40 or at 14:16, or what command she may have run.
That the approved update script was altered, contained malicious commands, or behaved maliciously.
That Dropbox or Google Drive was used to upload or exfiltrate organizational data.
That malicious activity occurred, or that all potentially relevant activity is represented in the supplied telemetry.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm with ivy.chen the approximate time and appearance of the reported window, and whether she recalls launching PowerShell.
Review endpoint process and console history around 13:40–14:20, including EDR telemetry, PowerShell operational logs, and any available command history.
Verify the contents, signature or hash, and execution audit trail for Apply-Updates.ps1 and confirm the patch action with sam.okafor.
Check software inventory and installation records for Dropbox and Google Drive, and review endpoint and proxy evidence for actual synchronization or file transfers.
